target_customer: Developer teams building internal tools, admin panels and B2B web apps in React, with an enterprise tier for companies needing SSO, access control and audit logging
problem: Building CRUD heavy internal apps repeats the same work on routing, auth, state and access control, and low-code tools like Retool lock teams into a hosted platform.
business_model: open-core: free open-source framework with paid enterprise and AI cloud features
product_category: open-source React framework for internal tools

founders.name: Civan Ozseyhan
founders.background_notes: YC page says serial entrepreneur with 15 plus years building enterprise software.

founders.name: Omer Aplak
education: University, dropped out in first year (school not named)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he started his software career in high school.

founders.name: Eren Erkalkan
founders.background_notes: YC page says he was Head of Product, founder and CEO in e-commerce and online dating for almost 15 years.

competitors.name: Retool
competitors.what: Hosted low-code platform for internal tools
competitors.funding_then: about $140M raised, last valued at $3.2B (per Sacra)

technical_complexity.rationale: A headless React framework with adapters for many backends and UI libraries is substantial but mainstream engineering for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Open source is copyable; the advantage is community size and ecosystem, and converting free users to paid has been hard per Sacra.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; the company moved from framework to an AI app generation platform in 2025.

market_need_then: Retool's growth to $82M ARR by end of 2022 showed heavy spend on internal tools, and some buyers wanted open-source and self-hosted options.

branding.domain_note: Uses refine.dev, a .dev domain, not a .com.
branding.brand_signature: Developer community: YC page cites 16K GitHub stars, 180 plus contributors and 2,500 Discord members

rebrands.why: Migration guide describes the move to the @refinedev organization with v4; the reason for the brand change is not stated.

branding.community_and_virality: Large open-source following with GitHub stars and a Discord community per the YC page; SD Times named it an open-source project of the week.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong developer community numbers and press as an open-source project, but a generic English word that is hard to search for.

pivots.to: AI agent app generator on top of the framework
pivots.why: Product Hunt lists an AI product launching June 19, 2025; the company site now leads with AI generated apps from existing APIs.

outcome_analysis: Refine built a large open-source community that gave it low cost distribution, then raised a $1M seed in 2022 and a $2.8M seed in May 2024 and pushed toward enterprise and AI products. Sacra notes converting free users to paid has been difficult, so monetization against Retool and Appsmith remained the open question.
notes: Two seed rounds recorded from Refine's own blog posts: $1M on 2022-06-10 led by 500 Istanbul and $2.8M on 2024-05-06 with Senovo and others. The 2024 post does not name a lead. Sacra shows $3.80M in 2024, which conflicts and was not confirmed. Rebrand year is not sourced precisely; the npm migration shows v4 under @refinedev.
